source: Tadros, Krishnan, Ramyaa, Bazhenov (2022) Sleep-like unsupervised replay reduces catastrophic forgetting in artificial neural networks
finding: After each task, the network goes offline. It gets noisy input, local Hebbian rules and synaptic scaling factors. This recovers old tasks that plain training erased. Parameters were tuned by a genetic algorithm on the training sets.
numbers: Two-task incremental test: without sleep first task 5%, second task 95%; with sleep 63.2% and 45.4%. CIFAR-10 overall 44% with sleep vs 19% without.
limits: Parameters (firing thresholds, scaling factors) tuned per dataset and architecture. Small networks; not language models.
agent_relevance: An offline pass between tasks that rebalances old against new is a plain analogue of a scheduled consolidation step. It needs a rebalance rule, not just more training.

source: Tadros, Krishnan, Ramyaa, Bazhenov (2022) Sleep-like unsupervised replay reduces catastrophic forgetting in artificial neural networks (comparison table)
finding: Sleep (SRC) is not the best continual-learning method on every set. OWM, a projection method, beat it on incremental MNIST.
numbers: Incremental MNIST: sequential training 19.49, EWC 20.37, SI 21.38, OWM 77.04, SRC 48.47 (+-5.03). Fashion MNIST: OWM 58.35, SRC 41.68.
limits: Sleep gives a partial fix. Seed spread is large (+-5).
agent_relevance: Do not expect a consolidation step to fully fix forgetting. Check it against a simple strong baseline.

source: Tadros, Krishnan, Ramyaa, Bazhenov (2022) Sleep-like unsupervised replay reduces catastrophic forgetting in artificial neural networks (iCaRL combination)
finding: Sleep adds to replay with stored examples. With a small buffer the gain is larger, and training time is saved.
numbers: MNIST: iCaRL K=100 65.5%, iCaRL+SRC 78.1%; K=200 76.9% vs 84.5%. K=1000: 87.7% after 8 epochs vs 87.32% after 10 epochs.
limits: Benefit is higher for low K and small at high K.
agent_relevance: Consolidation helps most when the raw memory buffer is small. This matters for a small lesson store.

source: Golden, Delanois, Sanda, Bazhenov (2022) Sleep prevents catastrophic forgetting in spiking neural networks by forming a joint synaptic weight representation
finding: New-task training moves weights off the old-task region. Interleaved sleep-like reactivation keeps weights near a region good for both tasks. The model includes homeostatic synaptic scaling toward a target input strength each epoch.
numbers: Qualitative weight-space analysis in a spiking network on a foraging task. No single headline percentage taken.
limits: Small spiking model; scaling is one fixed rule. Does not isolate scaling from replay.
agent_relevance: The goal of downselection can be a joint solution, not a deletion of old items.

source: Gonzalez, Sokolov, Krishnan, Delanois, Bazhenov (2020) Can sleep protect memories from catastrophic forgetting? (eLife)
finding: In a thalamocortical model, sleep replay after new learning reversed damage to old memories and let overlapping cells hold several memories. The model has no homeostatic rule, so net weight change depended on the STDP bias.
numbers: LTD-biased sleep gave net weight reduction; LTP-biased gave net increase. A peer reviewer said data of Mehta et al. fit net downscaling better than this model.
limits: Authors say extra homeostatic rules are needed before linking to Tononi and Cirelli.
agent_relevance: Replay-driven consolidation and global downscaling are separable. A model can show benefit without downscaling.

source: Krishnan, Tadros, Ramyaa, Bazhenov (2019) Biologically inspired sleep algorithm for artificial neural networks
finding: First sleep-like phase for feedforward networks: STDP rules plus raised activity after backprop. It recovers forgotten tasks, helps forward transfer, and helps noisy-image generalisation on MNIST, CUB200 and a toy set.
numbers: Abstract and introduction read; the main numbers are in the 2022 paper (c01 to c03).
limits: Early version; the 2022 paper is the better source.
agent_relevance: Shows the lineage: sleep as a post-training phase, not part of the loss.

source: Harun, Kanan (2023, TMLR) SIESTA: Efficient online continual learning with sleep
finding: Wake phase updates only the output layer, with no rehearsal. A sleep phase retrains the rest by replay. It matches an offline model without augmentation.
numbers: ImageNet-1K class-incremental, 12.5M updates: Offline final top-5 83.31; ER 63.92; REMIND 74.31; SIESTA 83.59 (mean 81.77). 1.9 h on one A5000 GPU. 2.19% of MobileNetV3-L is the wake part; 97.81% is trained in sleep.
limits: Sleep compute is capped by design. The result holds without augmentation.
agent_relevance: Cheap fast writes plus a heavier offline pass is a workable split for an agent: log fast, consolidate later.

source: Sorrenti et al. (2024) Wake-Sleep Consolidated Learning
finding: Wake, NREM (replay; plasticity strengthens important and weakens unimportant links) and REM (dreaming on unseen images). Ablations say each stage matters; REM drives forward transfer.
numbers: Final accuracy, buffer 200: ER 48.76 vs 51.86 with WSCL (CIFAR-10); DER++ 57.35 vs 63.97; ER-ACE 71.15. Without buffer (wake + REM) gains about 12% (Tiny-ImageNet) to 23% (CIFAR-10) over LwF, SI, oEWC.
limits: Table text garbled in extraction; only the first rows used. Image classification only. Forward transfer was negative for some pairs.
agent_relevance: Weaken-unimportant is one of three parts; credit is shared, so a single prune rule is not proven alone.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents
finding: Memory stream. Retrieval score = recency (exponential decay, factor 0.995) + importance (LLM-rated) + relevance. Reflection fires when summed importance passes a threshold and condenses memories upward.
numbers: Believability TrueSkill: full 29.89 (sd 0.72); no reflection 26.88; no reflection or planning 25.64; human crowdworkers 22.95; no memory, plan or reflection 21.21. d=8.16 vs prior-work baseline. 100 raters; Kruskal-Wallis chi2(4)=150.29, p<0.001.
limits: Nothing is deleted; decay only lowers rank. Believability, not task accuracy. No ablation of decay alone.
agent_relevance: Decay-ranked retrieval is a soft downscaling. Our schema can keep items but down-rank by age and use.

source: Zhong et al. (2023) MemoryBank
finding: Memory strength S starts at 1 and rises by 1 on each recall, with time reset. Retention R = exp(-t/S). Low-R items are forgotten. Authors call it exploratory and simplified.
numbers: 194 probe questions (97 English, 97 Chinese). English retrieval accuracy: ChatGLM 0.809, BELLE 0.814, ChatGPT 0.763; correctness ChatGPT 0.716.
limits: No test of the forgetting rule itself (no ablation). Users simulated by ChatGPT.
agent_relevance: Use-driven strength plus time decay is the simplest software form of the homeostasis idea; its gain is untested.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How memory management impacts LLM agents: experience-following
finding: Agents copy outputs of similar stored tasks, so errors in memory spread (error propagation). Deleting records by later utility (history-based) can beat no deletion, and even an error-free memory.
numbers: Strict evaluator, no deletion: RegAgent 70.95 (2938 records), EHRAgent 38.67 (1012), AgentDriver 51.00 (1178), CIC-IoT 85.40 (904). History-based: EHR 42.06 (784), AgentDriver 51.81 (846), CIC-IoT 89.60 (788). Combined: 42.34 (248), 49.97 (323), 85.50 (188).
quote: future task evaluations can serve as free quality labels for stored memory
limits: Table extracted with scrambled rows; assignment checked against the text. With the weak coarse evaluator, history deletion lost accuracy on one agent (78.10 to 68.80, CIC-IoT row). Needs a minimum retrieval count before deleting.
agent_relevance: Strongest direct test of pruning lessons. Prune by measured downstream utility, only after enough retrievals, and only with a reliable check.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) experience-following (periodic deletion)
finding: Periodic deletion by retrieval count and recency, a forgetting-rate rule from human cognition, cuts memory with small loss because add-only stores collect redundant entries.
numbers: Strict evaluator RegAgent: 70.95 with 2938 records vs about 67.65 with 949 under periodic deletion (row reading from scrambled table).
limits: Row reading is uncertain; text only says 'substantial memory reduction with small performance degradation'.
agent_relevance: A plain time-and-use decay is a cheap first prune rule; utility-based deletion is the better second.

source: Zhang et al. (2026, ICLR) Agentic Context Engineering (ACE)
finding: Playbook of bullets updated by small deltas. Counters are updated in place; a dedupe step prunes redundancy by embedding similarity. Full LLM rewrites cause context collapse.
numbers: Collapse case on AppWorld: at step 60 context 18,282 tokens, accuracy 66.7; next step 122 tokens, accuracy 57.1, below the no-adaptation 63.7. ACE gains +10.6% (agents), +8.6% (finance); adaptation latency down 86.9% on average.
limits: Weak without reliable feedback (ground truth or execution result); can be polluted by misleading signals.
agent_relevance: Prune with code (dedupe, counters); never let the model rewrite the whole store. Matches guardrail G5.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet
finding: A black-box model curates a short cheatsheet at test time: keep, refine or prune entries. Self-curated memory avoids context ballooning.
numbers: Game of 24 GPT-4o about 10% to 99% (DC-RS). AIME: Claude 3.5 Sonnet +27% (2024), +30% (2025) with DC-Cu. GPQA-Diamond +9%; MMLU-Pro Eng/Physics +8%.
limits: Small models (GPT-4o-mini) gain little: memory fills with wrong strategies and they cannot refine it. Much of the Game of 24 gain is one reused code snippet.
agent_relevance: Curation pays only when the model can make correct items first; gate memory writes on a pass.

source: Wang et al. (2024) Agent Workflow Memory
finding: Induces reusable workflows from past runs and supplies them selectively.
numbers: Relative success gain 24.6% (Mind2Web) and 51.1% (WebArena); gap-widening settings gain 8.9 to 14.0 absolute points. Abstract only read.
limits: Abstract read only; no pruning ablation extracted.
agent_relevance: Abstracted lessons beat raw trajectories when tasks shift.

source: Zhao et al. (2024) ExpeL
finding: The insight list is edited with ADD, EDIT, UPVOTE, DOWNVOTE; an insight whose score reaches zero is removed. Both insights and retrieval are needed.
numbers: HotpotQA: insights-only 36%, retrieve-only 31%. ALFWorld 50% / 55%. WebShop 37% / 38%. Against Reflexion: HotpotQA 40% vs 39%; ALFWorld 54% vs 59%. Transfer to FEVER: ReAct 58, ExpeL 70 (+-0.7).
limits: Value of insights depends on domain (insights matter on HotpotQA, trajectories on ALFWorld). Zero-removal rule read from the method text.
agent_relevance: A vote-based count of use is a ready prune rule for lessons.

source: Chhikara et al. (2025) Mem0
finding: For each extracted fact the model picks ADD, UPDATE, DELETE or NOOP. A selective store keeps accuracy near full context at far lower cost.
numbers: 26% relative gain on LLM-as-judge over OpenAI memory. Mem0 judge scores: single-hop 67.13, multi-hop 51.15, open-domain 72.93, temporal 55.51 (table-row reading). p95 latency down 91%, tokens down over 90% vs full context (judge 72.90).
limits: Zep scored higher on one category (judge 76.60). Judge is an LLM. Full context stays a strong accuracy baseline.
agent_relevance: DELETE and NOOP as first-class operations give most of the efficiency; accuracy is roughly kept while cost drops.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time compute
finding: An offline pass over the context before the query (anticipate questions, precompute). This is the replay side of sleep, not downscaling.
numbers: About 5x less test-time compute for equal accuracy. Scaling sleep compute: up to +13% (Stateful GSM-Symbolic) and +18% (Stateful AIME). 10 queries per context: 2.5x lower cost per query. SWE-Features: about 1.5x fewer test tokens.
limits: At high test budgets plain test-time compute wins (extra context distracts). 5 parallel sleep generations beat 10. Works only when queries are predictable.
agent_relevance: A pause step that rewrites memory before the next task pays only when the next task is predictable from the context.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time compute (predictability)
finding: Gain from sleep-time work tracks how predictable the question is from the context. Binned by predictability, accuracy gain rises with predictability.
numbers: Five predictability bins on GSM-Symbolic P1 and P2 with GPT-4o-mini; delta rises with bin.
limits: Predictability measured with a language-model score; one model.
agent_relevance: Spend consolidation compute only where future queries are predictable; otherwise save the tokens.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) ACE (ablation)
finding: Each part adds to AppWorld score: reflector, multi-epoch adaptation, offline warmup. Weak or noisy reflectors still stay above the base model except under harmful signals.
numbers: Online adaptation rows: ReAct + ACE gives gains of +4.2 to +24.5 points across splits depending on setting.
limits: Numbers are from a scrambled table; use only the range.
agent_relevance: Curate from execution signals, not from model opinion.

source: Suzgun et al. (2025) Dynamic Cheatsheet (limits)
finding: A cheatsheet with an empty memory but the same prompt scores much lower than one with memory, so gains are not only from the prompt.
numbers: DC- (no memory) 19% on one task versus DC variants far higher; Haiku-class models gain little.
limits: Authors list context and memory curation limits for smaller models.
agent_relevance: Control for the prompt when testing a memory step.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager
finding: Skill library of code, stored only after a self-check says the task passed. The library only grows.
numbers: 3.3x more unique items, 2.3x longer distances, tech tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than the prior best.
limits: No pruning study; abstract and intro read.
agent_relevance: Gate on a pass before writing; an append-only store sufficed in this domain.

source: Xu et al. (2025) A-MEM: Agentic memory
finding: Zettelkasten-style notes with links; new notes can rewrite attributes of old ones (memory evolution). Intro and method text read.
numbers: No numbers extracted.
limits: No delete step; drift from repeated rewriting not measured here.
agent_relevance: In-place rewrite is the opposite of downscaling and risks collapse (see ACE).

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT
finding: Paged memory for LLM context with self-managed eviction and summarisation. PDF fetched, not read.
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: Unread; lineage only.
agent_relevance: Eviction by recursive summary is the older design.

source: Tadros et al. (2022) Sleep-like unsupervised replay (mechanism)
finding: During sleep old-task classes were replayed spontaneously with unique representations per class. Sparseness and old-task activity rose while new-task activity fell.
numbers: Qualitative (abstract and results text).
limits: Mechanism shown in small ReLU-to-spiking-style networks.
agent_relevance: The useful effect was lowering the dominance of the newest task, which maps to down-weighting recent lessons that crowd out older ones.
